newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-PONTING AND ELLIOTT BRING AUSTRALIA CLOSER TO ASHES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-PONTING AND ELLIOTT BRING AUSTRALIA CLOSER TO ASHES.

text.p: Australia took a firm grip on the fourth test against England at Headingley on Saturday, with Ricky Ponting completing his maiden test century and opener Matthew Elliott batting through the first session on the third day to reach 164 not out.
When rain stopped play four balls early, the Australians were 373 for five in their first innings, 201 ahead.
Their only worry, and England's only hope, was in the local weather forecast, predicting persistent rain for the afternoon.
The day began in bright sunshine, during which Ponting reached his 100, survived a botched stumping off Robert Croft and then skied Darren Gough to backward point, where Mark Ealham took the catch.

The Tasmanian had faced 202 balls for his 127, made in his first match against England, with 19 fours and one six. His splendid innings was something of a rebuke for the selectors, who had dropped him soon after he scored 88 against the West Indies last November and ignored him ever since. The stand with Elliott, begun when Australia were tottering at 50 for four, produced 268 in only 263 minutes to leave England with virtually no hope of regaining the lead in the series with two matches to play.

There was no respite for them, despite taking the new ball. Ian Healy helped himself to two fours off his first three balls and had 27 by lunch. Elliott, dropped on 29, had already reached the highest score of his 15 test innings.
Michael Atherton rotated his bowlers, but there was little turn for off-spinner Robert Croft and little swing for Mike Smith, who remained wicketless on his debut.
